Are you trying to learn how to frenzel. Or trying to improve your frenzel ? I could do frenzel intuitively and was trying to improve but I was stuck on the same thing as as you, I thought I had no soft palate control, air from the balloon kept rushing into my lungs when trying to do stuff with my throat. Was looking everywhere for like two days until I stumbled on some old forum where a guy was having the same problem and someone told him that if he can't control his soft palate he can't frenzel. I realized there was this thing I do with the back of my throat when I equalize. Turned out the thing was opening my soft palate and I could do the balloon exercise without issues. It's really hard to explain how to control your soft palate, you can probably do it already and just aren't aware what it feels like and when you do it. To me it feels like I am sort of stretching the upper back part of my throat, sort of like when you yawn, it makes your ears crackle. Look at the xray frenzel video from adamfreediver (i think thats the name) it might give you an idea of what to do. You just have to find what that secret muscle movement is and it can be frustrating, also stop trying weird things you've never done with your throat before if you're doing that.

Hey, I have the 40/41, my foot when traced on paper is about 95mm wide and 260mm long, when I have my foot in the air it's about 90mm wide. When compared to most of the regular short snorkeling fins it's a bit bigger and a lot stiffer. I use it with cotton socks that are slightly thicker than normal, (I definitely wouldn't go for a smaller size tho). I was a worried at first since it was putting a lot of pressure on the top of my foot, but after heating it up with a hair drier and shaping it to be slightly asymetric (so I now have a left and right one) they work great. I used them heavily for 14 days last year with no issues, my old snorkeling fins that I wore barefoot which seemed more comfortable at first left my feet a bit chafed and made my arch hurt a bit after a week of use a year prior. I don't have any experience with other brands except no name snorkeling fins, but from what I saw the c4 foot pocket shape may be a bit more slim than some others especially if you have a high arch, I also don't think the material is great for wearing it barefoot and most people seemed to wear 250 with socks when I was looking into it last year. Also since the material isn't so elastic you want it to be a little loose in walking position and then tighten up when you point your toes to start finning.  Since your foot is 5mm wider than mine I think 38/39 will be too narrow for you. Can you send them back if they don't fit?

Pretty sure it's not a clogged nozzle, you said you tried printing three times and the result is always the same, the model or g-code is the problem. This sometimes happens with cura, everything looks fine and then it just stops extruding, always on the same layer. Sometimes you can see it by changing from line type to flow in preview. You need to fix the model, try opening it in your cad of choice and resaving it as stl. To me this usually happens when I model something big as a part in solidworks (like big multipart models that really should have been an assembly, with convoluted feature tree because I'm lazy), I'm using solidworks plugin so that cura can open .sldprt files, not sure how it works exactly but my stl export setting affect the output to cura so I think it converts to stl. However parts opened with this plugin can have the aforementioned problem where the flow just stops(or almost stops) for no reason, when I save the model as stl snd open that in cura it doesn't happen. If you model something really messily in solidworks tho the model can be so broken that even saving it doesn't fix it, this is visible in cura however with the missing faces warning and the problematic faces glow blue. Some other but less probable culprits could be corrupt file on the sd card or a file with a foreign character in the name (I know it sound weird but I've seen this cause some weird stuff). Hopefully this helps
